label: jex-n8-v16
_why: THE SAME BOOK AS 20261005_154629_jex-n16, EIGHT MORE CENTURIES ON SAVE SUMMARY v16 (user, 2026-10-06: 'Go on with another n=8 on the new telemetry. After the first four runs, run a preliminary analysis on the fleet / excess slowdown correlation.'). The book config/mod_config.e1a12-ai1135-tex1140-jex-artmerge.json is unchanged; what differs is the harvest: v16 summaries carry, per country and world-wide, the military formations and their travel paths (moves, distance sailed, recalled fleets, loops = recalled AND >= 200 moves, the worst 40 paths with owner id, repair target, top-2-node share, ships), so a slowdown seen in the observer's ticks can be read against the fleets that were sailing that year, not only against the run's newest kept save. The jex-n16 report was deferred by the user to after this batch: both batches are read together (n=8 + n=8 of one book) for the research questions, then FINDINGS. A FIXED-n batch: every run plays 1836 -> 1936, no stop watcher.

_arms.jex: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.e1a12-ai1135-tex1140-jex-artmerge.json} (+ its tree twin). Identical to the jex arm of 20261005_154629.

_comparison: Research and economy: pooled with 20261005_154629 runs 1-8 (same book), against the control e1a12-ai1135-tex1140 (20261003_171038, n=5) and the canon (20260929_002728). Wall clock: fleet_loop_runs.mjs per run (disqualified share and the qualifying play time) against vanilla n=16 + the eleven-tag set; slow_episodes.mjs for the factorised branches; machine_monitor.ps1 (started by run_schedule) for the machine side.

_questions.F1 FLEET vs EXCESS (preliminary at run 4: Per run and in-game year: the excess seconds per in-game year over the batch's median pace for that year (tick_profile.mjs / the observer's ticks, autosave ticks out), against the v16 world.formations readings of the same year — loops, recalled fleets, moves, dist, dist_k2, and the worst paths' distance. Does the excess track distance sailed by looping/recalled fleets (F218's cost-vs-distance shape: <=125k ~0-10 s/yr, ~150-200k ~20-30 s, ~470k ~100-200 s)? Is it carried by the sub-tick the looping owner's id mod 4 maps to (F218 sec. 8)? What share of the excess is NOT explained by fleets (wars: all sub-ticks rising)?
_questions.F2 THE SHARE: Do the entries make loops likelier? jex-n16 read 3 of 8 runs disqualified against ~8% in the corpus; eight more runs say whether that was luck.

_predictions.F1: Where a run has a fleet-loop episode, the year's excess rises with the looping fleets' distance sailed (dist_k2 the better predictor, cost superlinear in path length) and sits on one sub-tick; years with no recalled path above ~150k carry under ~10 s of excess unless a great-power war is running. Most excess outside loops is war, lifting all four sub-ticks.
_predictions.F2: 1-3 of 8 runs disqualified; if 3+ again, the entries plausibly raise the loop rate (more naval technology earlier -> more fleets abroad), to be checked against when the loop's ships were built.

_stop_rule: none: a fixed n=8, every run plays to 1936. Only a hard harness failure (crash loop, mod not loaded) stops it.
_cost: 8 runs x 1836 -> 1936, about 2.5-4.5 h each, about 22-30 h
_caveats: Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30).
Do NOT edit tools/testbed/save_state_summary.mjs while the batch runs: the harvester loads it per save, so an edit mid-batch changes what later summaries carry.
Do NOT edit tools/emit_research_events.mjs, tools/make_research_extra_config.mjs, tools/emit_secondaries.mjs or the book while the batch runs: the mod is rebuilt before every run.

Yearly saves only: a loop that starts and ends between two yearly saves is seen in the ticks but not in the formations reading; when a run slows mid-batch, copy its newest save into diag_saves/ before the harvester reaps it.
run_schedule.ps1 adds the red-flag feed (market_goods_wide each 1 July) and the machine-load monitor.
